question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: an MCP initialize (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-registry-probe 1.0) with Accept application/json and text/event-stream; then tools/list twice, once carrying the returned mcp-session-id and once with no session header; then prompts/list and resources/list; then a plain GET; then an initialize with the clientInfo key removed

decoded.serverInfo: Microsoft Learn MCP Server 1.0.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, capabilities logging{}, prompts.listChanged true, resources.listChanged true, tools.listChanged true. The instructions string is 1522 characters and names three tools, which is what tools/list serves (artifact sections A and G)
decoded.session-id-is-not-opaque: the mcp-session-id header is a 224-character plain base64 envelope, no signature segment, which decodes to {"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-registry-probe","title":null,"version":"1.0","icons":null,"websiteUrl":null},"userIdClaim":"e19aa6d8-d2b8-4503-b940-ff4683c9ee22"}. The caller's own clientInfo is echoed back verbatim inside a header value, so an agent's client name and version travel where every intermediary on the path can read them
decoded.userIdClaim-is-per-session: five initializes from this one egress address inside five minutes returned five different UUIDs (e19aa6d8, b0f1a0a0, aa6f64b1, 0f30d6f8, c384b513, full values in artifact section B), one of them under a different clientInfo name. The field is named userIdClaim, which reads like a persistent identity; measured, it is minted per initialize and is not a stable identifier for this caller
decoded.session-not-required: tools/list answered 200 with no mcp-session-id header at all, and both bodies were 4950 bytes (artifact section C). The session the server mints is not needed to call it
decoded.capabilities-with-nothing-behind-them: prompts/list returns {"prompts":[]} and resources/list returns {"resources":[]}, both 200, against an initialize that advertises prompts.listChanged true and resources.listChanged true
decoded.plain-GET: 405 Method Not Allowed with an HTML page reading "This is an MCP server endpoint and cannot be accessed directly via a...". The vendor's overview page predicts this: "It does not support direct access from a web browser and may return a 405 Method Not Allowed error if accessed manually"
decoded.no-clientInfo: HTTP 500 with a plain-text, non-JSON-RPC body: "JSON deserialization for type 'ModelContextProtocol.Protocol.InitializeRequestParams' was missing required properties including: 'clientInfo'." Refusing is correct, since the MCP specification requires clientInfo; what is recorded is the shape. An unknown tool name on the same server gets a proper JSON-RPC -32602 inside a 200
decoded.no-quota-header: the complete set of header names observed on any response in this pass is akamai-cache-status, cache-control, content-encoding, content-length, content-type, date, expires, mcp-session-id, nel, report-to, request-context, set-cookie, strict-transport-security, x-azure-ref, x-content-type-options, x-powered-by. No ratelimit, quota or retry-after header of any kind
decoded.not-measured: whether any server-side state attaches to a session id that IS presented; whether the server correlates callers by another means; and any rate limit, which was deliberately not probed by volume

finding: With no credentials and no payment on 2026-09-30, the Microsoft Learn MCP Server answered initialize, tools/list, prompts/list and resources/list with 200, serving three read-only tools. Two things a caller should know are not in any vendor page. The mcp-session-id it issues is not opaque: it is plain base64 of a JSON object that echoes the caller's clientInfo verbatim and adds a UUID named userIdClaim, which five initializes in five minutes showed is minted per session rather than persistent; and tools/list answers with no session header at all, so the session is optional. Two advertised capabilities, prompts and resources, list nothing. An initialize missing clientInfo answers HTTP 500 with a plain-text .NET deserialization message rather than a JSON-RPC error, while an unknown tool name on the same server answers -32602 correctly.
